title: OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect & Policy Authorization
description: Secure ASP.NET Core and React applications with OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWT validation, and custom claims-based authorization policies.

data.text: The Security Architecture of Modern Web & AI Applications

Authentication verifies who a user is; Authorization determines what they are allowed to do. In modern distributed architectures, authentication is externalized to an Identity Provider (such as Microsoft Entra ID, Auth0, or Okta) using OpenID Connect (OIDC), while delegated authorization is governed by OAuth 2.0 access tokens. For AI applications, authorization must not only protect API endpoints, but also govern which documents the user can retrieve from vector databases and which tools an agent can execute on their behalf.
Validating JWT Bearer Tokens in ASP.NET Core

Every incoming HTTP request to an AI endpoint must present a cryptographically verified JSON Web Token (JWT). The ASP.NET Core JWT Bearer authentication handler validates cryptographic signatures using asymmetric public keys fetched from the identity provider's JWKS endpoint.

data.title: Configuring JWT Bearer Authentication in Program.cs
data.content: Configures strict signature, audience, and lifetime validation:

rows: Static roles assigned to user: Admin, User, Viewer
Restricting access to admin configuration dashboards
Vector database query filtering; ensuring users only retrieve departmental knowledge
C# requirements and handlers evaluating multiple contextual claims
Verifying whether an agent tool invocation is permitted for the current user

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use OpenID Connect (OIDC) for user identity and OAuth 2.0 for API access delegation
Always validate JWT signatures, issuers, audiences, and lifetimes in ASP.NET Core
Never rely solely on coarse roles: use fine-grained claims for data filtering
Extract tenant and department claims to enforce server-side vector query partitioning
Gate sensitive AI tool execution behind specific OAuth scopes (ai.tools.execute)
data.takeaway: Authentication and authorization provide the perimeter defense for enterprise systems. Validating JWT claims and enforcing policy-based authorization protects both API endpoints and underlying AI tools.
